external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: Customer who browses and orders through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application used by customers to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: API used by the mobile app, storing customer information and handing orders to SIMS. The API changes prices and product copy when addressed by spreadsheet macros.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: Stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS, our stock and inventory system

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the catalogue spreadsheet that send SQL statements directly to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: Gateway that sends dispatch notes by fax to the number stored against an order.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation
processes.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: Database containing customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database ... [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: File kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me ... whether the ... flat file [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: catalogue spreadsheet
data_stores.description: Spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue, including prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_stores.name: marketing laptop
data_stores.description: Laptop in the office where the catalogue spreadsheet resides.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering through the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Mobile app communication with the web API for browsing and placing orders.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.description: Web API stores customer names, addresses, and payment card information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and payment card information

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.description: Web API hands an order to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: Fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: Spreadsheet macros send SQL statements directly to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: customer device
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary around the customer's mobile device running the mobile app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

trust_boundaries.name: Sokify
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary around Sokify's API, inventory system, data stores, marketing laptop, and fax gateway.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a mobile app and explicitly says there is no website.
SIMS is described as a stock and inventory system, not a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The spreadsheet macros present a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: They are macros in a spreadsheet rather than a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The fax gateway presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a fax gateway that dials a number and faxes a confirmation.
Sokify sells online and the customer mobile app communicates with the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The user database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file contains confidential data.
